data.long_meaning: A person who gives alms or charities, provides sustenance for the needy, and fulfills their obligations. The name Sadqan carries the meaning “One who gives alms” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Arabic. Parents who choose Sadqan usually hope their child will grow to embody one who gives alms and live with faith, good character and purpose.

data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Sadqan total 2, giving a life-path number of 2. Number 2 is linked with Moon and with the qualities of harmony, sensitivity and partnership.
data.cultural_impact: In Islamic culture, the term "Sadqan" holds great significance as it refers to a person who is generous, altruistic, and prioritizes giving to those in need over personal gains. This concept is deeply ingrained in Islamic society, which values community, compassion, and social justice. The male name Sadqan highlights the character traits of a kind-hearted, charitable individual.
data.spiritual_significance: In the spiritual realm, the name Sadqan symbolizes a deep connection with Allah and a commitment to living out the Islamic values of compassion, generosity, and righteousness. The name is a reminder to fulfill one's obligations to others and to Allah, and to strive towards creating positive change in the world. Sadqan's spiritual significance is a call to live a life of giving, selflessness, and service to others.

historical_references.context: Sadqan ibn Mu'adh Al-Khudri was a well-known companion of the Prophet (pbuh) and a judge during the caliphate of Umar ibn Al-Khattab. He was renowned for his honesty and piety.

historical_references.reference: Historical records show that Al-Bukhari - Sahih Bukhari (Vol. 8, Book 73, No. 8) The name Sadqan carried significant weight in that era.
historical_references.time_period: The time of the Prophet Muhammad (pbuh)
historical_references.context: The Prophet (pbuh) called Sadqan ibn Mu'adh Al-Khudri, while he was sitting in the mosque, and said, 'O Sadqan!' He replied, 'Labas Allah wa 'adan (May Allah bless you and grant you increase in good) O Messenger of Allah!' The Prophet (pbuh) said, 'I have been given the keys of Paradise and Hell, and I will not enter Paradise before my Ummah has entered it. I will not enter Hell before my Ummah has been saved from it. And I will not enter Paradise until my Ummah has been gathered together. Then I will enter it and my Ummah will follow me.' Sadqan said, 'O Messenger of Allah! Will we be gathered together after you?' He (pbuh) replied, 'Yes, by the One in Whose Hands my soul is!'

modern_usage.modern_context: Sadqan is an Arabic term used in Islamic finance and charitable giving, referring to alms-giving or donations to worthy causes. It's seen on various platforms such as ZakatHub, an app and website that helps Muslims calculate and distribute their zakat (a form of charitable giving), Meezan Bank, one of the largest Islamic banks in Pakistan, and PayPal, a digital payment platform, which makes it easier for individuals to donate to their preferred charities around the world. Sadqan is also becoming increasingly popular in the context of digital wallets, as more people turn to online methods for making charitable contributions.
